evidence: Ran python3 -I test_disposition_completeness.py at commit d67e3c8a: 26/26 tests passed (exit 0). Built a self-contained (no cross-unit import) disposition-completeness checker that discovers superseded files by scanning JSON/JSONL supersession keys, then checks each against three structured disposition sources: inline standing fields, operations/INSTRUCTION_ESTATE_DISPOSITION_20260819_v001.md table rows, and verified high_risk_markers from scripts/check_operator_taxonomy.py. Real-repo run (real_repo_run.json) found 58 superseded files across 386 scanned JSON/JSONL files: 24 dispositioned via inline standing, 0 rescued by the disposition table (which names only 1 explicit path) or verified markers (5 paths, all disjoint from the 34), leaving 34 of 58 (59%) as precisely-named open defects. Byte-identity tests confirm the checker never mutates any scanned file, on both a synthetic fixture repo and the real repository's state/ACTIVE_CONTROL_POINTER_CURRENT.json.
falsifiable_hypothesis: Every superseded file either carries an explicit disposition or is reported as an open defect.
limitations: Only three structured disposition sources are recognised (inline standing, disposition table, verified high_risk_markers); a file with an informal disposition in some other narrative field (e.g. migration_ref) is correctly reported as an open defect rather than silently credited, per the fail-closed design.
